> v4.6.2 is the next patch release.

## 👉 Changelog

[compare changes](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/compare/v4.6.1...v4.6.2)

### 🩹 Fixes

- **nitro:** apply `useHeadSafe` rules to server island head ([`493565e99`](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/commit/493565e99))
- **nitro-server:** read router params from the path h3 matched ([`010f6b43d`](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/commit/010f6b43d))
- **nitro:** match server route rules case-insensitively unless routing is sensitive ([`f6cfee52c`](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/commit/f6cfee52c))
- **nuxt:** resolve rooted paths through the URL parser (#36617)
- **nuxt:** resolve empty route types in shared context (#36576)
- **nitro:** preserve server tsconfig with relocated build dir (#36494)
- **nuxt:** fix scroll offset for IDs starting with numbers (#36524)
- **kit:** do not exclude module directories with a dot in their name from app tsconfig (#36331)
- **nuxt:** detect vapor slots with `rawVaporSlotKey` from vue (#36614)
- **nuxt:** keep middleware layout when restoring deferred prerendered route (#36560)
- **schema:** provide default value for `experimental.typescriptPlugin` (#36561)
- **vite:** only replay compile error overlays to newly loaded pages (#36611)
- **nuxt:** re-export `AnyFetchPath` for emitted server route types (#36610)
- **vite:** warm up the dev ssr entry from a nitro plugin (#36615)
- **nitro:** avoid unused h3 imports in nuxt/server runtime (#36609)
- **vite-server:** scope asset url helpers to the build (#36591)
- **nuxt:** resolve `nuxt/app` to the app's runtime (#36587)
- **kit:** lowercase filename-derived handler method on nitro v2 (#36567)
- **nuxt,nitro:** normalise string/array `appMiddleware` (#36565)
- **nitro:** pass response headers to `render:response` listeners (#36583)
- **vite:** resolve inlined `vue` to its bundler build in dev (#36569)
- **nuxt:** don't start a page transition with no page to leave (#36535)
- **nuxt:** preserve error state on aborted or cancelled navigation (#36546)
- **vite,nitro:** link null-byte virtual css through `/@id/` in dev (#36549)
- **kit:** resolve module dependencies from the declaring module (#36542)
- **nitro:** only disable h3 + nitro presets when `nitroAutoImports` is off (#36548)
- **nitro,vite:** don't access unspecified dependencies (#36541)
- **nitro:** don't inline deps under absolute transpile dirs (#36540)
- **vite-server:** respect spa loading template location (#36536)

### 💅 Refactors

- **webpack,rspack:** inline friendly errors plugin (#36568)

### 📖 Documentation

- remove DeepWiki badge (#36616)
- rename `H(TTP)` to `HTTP` (#36559)
- mention `proxy` route rule ([`4a529be68`](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/commit/4a529be68))

prs.title: fix(nitro): mark legacy `event.$fetch` sub-requests when rendering errors
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

### 📚 Description

this PR marks sub-requests made while rendering an error page with `~rendering-error`, which is the same context the error handler already passes to its own `/__nuxt_error` fetch.

this stops hanging forever if calling `event.$fetch` when rendering an error page

prs.title: fix(schema): give experimental.typescriptPlugin its documented default
prs.author: Neekoras
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

None, found while comparing `ExperimentalOptions` against the resolvers.

### 📚 Description

`experimental.typescriptPlugin` is the only one of the 62 experimental options with no entry in `packages/schema/src/config/experimental.ts`. It is declared `typescriptPlugin: boolean` in `ExperimentalOptions` and documented as `@default false`, and `nuxt.ts` reads it, but nothing gives it a default, so it resolves to `undefined` and the key is absent from the resolved config:

```js
const { experimental } = await loadNuxtConfig({ cwd })

experimental.typescriptPlugin                       // undefined
Object.hasOwn(experimental, 'typescriptPlugin')     // false
experimental.extractAsyncDataHandlers               // false, like every other flag
```

With this change it resolves to `false` and the key is present, so the resolved options match the type and the documented default. It uses the same `$resolve` shape as its neighbours, which also coerce a non-boolean to the default rather than passing it through.

Nothing changes for anyone setting the flag, and nothing changes behaviourally for the default either, since `if (options.experimental.typescriptPlugin)` already treated `undefined` as off. What changes is that code reading the option gets the boolean its type promises, and that the flag appears when the resolved experimental options are enumerated.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): keep middleware layout when restoring deferred prerendered route
prs.author: kazbekaskarov
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Resolves #36429

### 📚 Description

During hydration of a prerendered page with query parameters, `restoreDeferredRoute` replaces the current route with a freshly resolved route. This discards the route metadata set by middleware via `setPageLayout`, causing `NuxtLayout` to resolve a different layout. Since the resolved layout name is used as the key for the internal `LayoutProvider`, this can trigger unnecessary remounts during hydration and potentially break async components inside the layout.

This PR:

- preserves the hydrated route's `meta` when restoring a deferred route, keeping middleware-set layout values (e.g. `setPageLayout('custom')`) instead of reverting to static page metadata (e.g. `layout: false`).
- adds regression tests for prerendered pages with and without query parameters, verifying that the original server-rendered layout and page DOM nodes are reused after hydration.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): detect vapor slots with `rawVaporSlotKey` from vue
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

resolves #36566

### 📚 Description

https://github.com/vuejs/core/pull/15355 replaced the `__vapor`/`__vs` string markers with a `rawVaporSlotKey` symbol, which broke our implementation.

we now use the `rawVaporSlotKey` symbol. it's exported from `vue` but doesn't exist in 3.5, so we have a little bit of indirection until v3.6 is released and we can bump our dependency

prs.title: fix(kit): do not exclude module directories with a dot in their name from app tsconfig
prs.author: dsfcoll
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

resolves https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/36330

### 📚 Description

This replaces the bare `*.*` globs with one glob per extension from `nuxt.options.extensions`. The same change applies to the `layers/*/modules` globs and the per-module excludes in the app, node and server tsconfigs.

Example for a project with `modules/1.first/` and `modules/plain/`, extensions trimmed for brevity.

**Before**, `.nuxt/tsconfig.app.json`:

```json
"exclude": [
  "../modules/*.*",
  "../modules/1.first/*.*",
  "../modules/plain/*.*"
]
```

**After**:

```json
"exclude": [
  "../modules/*.mjs",
  "../modules/*.js",
  "../modules/*.ts",
  "../modules/*.vue",
  "../modules/1.first/*.mjs",
  "../modules/1.first/*.js",
  "../modules/1.first/*.ts",
  "../modules/1.first/*.vue",
  "../modules/plain/*.mjs",
  "../modules/plain/*.js",
  "../modules/plain/*.ts",
  "../modules/plain/*.vue"
]
```

P.S. Maybe it is a good idea to also add a fixture with a dotted module directory?

prs.title: fix(nuxt): fix scroll offset for IDs starting with numbers
prs.author: ozenyunus35
prs.body:
Linked issue

Fixes #36460

Description

* Problem: document.querySelector('#5-tips') throws an error because the hash is not a valid CSS selector. As a result, Nuxt calculates a scroll offset of 0 instead of respecting scroll-margin-top.
* Fix: Replace the selector lookup with document.getElementById() to find the target element directly.
* Regression coverage: Add tests for a regular ID (section) and a digit-leading ID (5-tips).

Testing

* Runtime tests: 1,024 passed
* TypeScript: passed
* ESLint on changed files: passed
* Full test suite: not run

AI assistance

Claude Code (Opus 5.5) assisted with implementation and testing.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): resolve empty route types in shared context
prs.author: dargmuesli
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

resolves #36575

### 📚 Description

`nuxt/app`'s fetch types import the generated `server-routes.d.ts`, which loads every server handler with `typeof import(...)`. So once anything in `shared/` reaches `nuxt/app`, the shared program type-checks the handlers too, but it doesn't reference the server auto-import declarations, and handlers fail with `Cannot find name 'defineEventHandler'`.

This adds the server auto-import declarations and `types/nitro-nuxt.d.ts` to the shared references, mirroring the server program. The second one is needed because the server-imports declarations lead into nuxt's renderer, which relies on the `import.meta.test` augmentation. On `main` this only shows up with `nitroAutoImports` enabled, which the basic-types fixture has.

The trade-off is that code in `shared/` can now also see Nitro's auto-import globals, the same as the app context already does. The alternative would be stubbing `#build/server-routes` for the shared program, which drops route typing there.

The new test in the basic-types fixture imports a handler from `shared/` and fails without this change. I opened #36577 for 4.x, where the fix is a single reference.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): resolve rooted paths through the URL parser
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

### 📚 Description

this was a regression from https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36459: values like `/\t/example.com` were classified as rooted paths

this PR keeps the fast check, but when the character after the leading `/` is a tab, LF or CR, we fall back to the same URL parse `isAbsoluteHref` uses.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): don't warn for vite+ `vite.config` files
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

https://github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/issues/1506

### 📚 Description

this suppresses the warning about `vite.config.ts` when it's a vite-plus config file, which is totally fine to use alongside nuxt...

prs.title: fix(nitro): call `nitro:build:public-assets` before building nitro env
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

### 📚 Description

this is a workaround until the next nitro release and a new `vite:compile:before` hook...

with `experimental.nitroViteEnvironment` enabled, files a module writes into the public output in `nitro:build:public-assets` end up on disk but aren't served in a production build.

for example, `@vite-pwa/nuxt` writes `sw.js` and `workbox-*.js` in this hook....

prs.title: fix(nuxt): let nightly runtime resolve its own `nuxt/*` imports
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

### 📚 Description

on the 5.x nightly, importing `nuxt/server` outside a Nuxt build would fail, because we import our own stubs as `nuxt/internal/*`, but the nightly is published as `nuxt-nightly`.

this adds a nuxt -> nuxt-nightly alias when packed so `nuxt` is linked/accessible to the stubs.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): avoid self-referencing `nuxt/schema` augmentation
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

### 📚 Description

our types currently didn't resolve properly (but this was ignored as we skipped lib checking)

this resolves an issue where modules augmenting `nuxt/schema` could have their augmentations ignored

this PR maps `nuxt/schema` to the same path as `@nuxt/schema` in the generated tsconfigs, so the two names are one module and every augmentation lands in the same place.

(and we also then have to avoid another self-referencing situation)
